studies.title: Off-label prescribing of psychotropic drugs in a Danish child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic
studies.medication_focus: Psychotropic drugs (including ADHD medications like methylphenidate)
studies.dosing_strategy: Off-label use regarding age and indication
studies.key_findings: Found that 32.7% of patients received at least one off-label prescription. Methylphenidate was among the most common off-label drugs, often prescribed to children outside the approved age range.

studies.title: Off-Label Prescription of Psychopharmacological Drugs in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry in Denmark
studies.key_findings: High prevalence of off-label prescribing (44%) in clinical practice. The study highlights that off-label use is common for ADHD medications in younger children (under 6) and for comorbid conditions.

studies.title: Use of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder medication among adults aged >=50 years in Denmark
studies.key_findings: Observed a 10-fold increase in ADHD medication use among adults aged 50+ years between 2005 and 2015, highlighting a shift towards off-label age group prescribing as diagnosis in adults grows.

studies.title: Drug therapy of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
studies.dosing_strategy: Off-label use of non-stimulants and antidepressants
studies.key_findings: While methylphenidate is the gold standard, the study supports off-label use of atomoxetine, tricyclic antidepressants, and alpha-agonists (like clonidine) in Indian clinical settings, especially when stimulants are ineffective or poorly tolerated.

studies.title: A Review of Long-Acting Medications for ADHD in Canada
studies.journal_name: Journal of the Canadian Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
studies.medication_focus: Methylphenidate ER, Mixed Amphetamine Salts XR, Atomoxetine
studies.dosing_strategy: Multiple doses per day (IR) vs Extended-release
studies.key_findings: Discusses that before the availability of long-acting agents, multiple daily doses of immediate-release medications were the standard. It supports the clinical practice of using IR boosters to manage 'rebound' or cover evening activities.

studies.title: Trends in attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder medication use: a retrospective observational study using population-based databases
studies.region: Northern Europe (UK, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland), Canada
studies.dosing_strategy: Global trends including off-label adult prescribing
studies.key_findings: The study found significant increases in ADHD medication prescribing for adults across Northern Europe and Canada, despite many medications not having initial adult labels, indicating widespread off-label adult use.

studies.title: Low to moderate-dose off-label use of second-generation antipsychotics in child and adolescent psychiatry
studies.dosing_strategy: Off-label adjunct therapy for ADHD symptoms
studies.key_findings: In Finland, 40% of children prescribed off-label low-dose antipsychotics were concurrently taking ADHD medication, using the antipsychotics to manage aggressive behavior or sleep issues associated with ADHD.

studies.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder medication consumption in 64 countries and regions, 2015–2019: a longitudinal study
studies.dosing_strategy: Trends in consumption and off-label usage
studies.key_findings: Reported an 18.08% annual increase in ADHD medication consumption in Northern Europe. It notes that while labels vary, clinical use often involves off-label indications for adults and comorbid management.

studies.title: The Use of Medication Against Attention deficit/hyperactivity Disorder in Denmark: A Drug Use Study From a Patient Perspective
studies.key_findings: Dropout rates were highest among off-label users. However, the study confirms that off-label use (under 6 and adults) is a significant part of the prescribing landscape in Denmark.

studies.title: Off-label prescription of psychopharmacological drugs for children and adolescents
studies.key_findings: Confirmed that approximately 30-40% of prescriptions in Danish child psychiatry are off-label. ADHD medications are frequently prescribed to preschool children (off-label age).

studies.title: Potential Role of Dexamphetamine in the Treatment of Non-ADHD Conditions
studies.journal_name: Journal of Postgraduate Medicine, Education and Research
studies.key_findings: Highlights that dexamphetamine, primarily an ADHD drug, is used off-label in India for conditions like refractory depression and fatigue, showing the flexibility of ADHD stimulants in clinical practice.

studies.title: A study of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children and adolescents in a tertiary care psychiatric hospital in North India
studies.dosing_strategy: Clinical medication patterns (including IR methylphenidate multiple doses)
studies.key_findings: In India, immediate-release methylphenidate is common and often requires multiple daily doses (2-3 times/day) to maintain therapeutic efficacy throughout the day, as long-acting versions were less accessible.

studies.title: Adult ADHD and its comorbidities, with a focus on alcohol and drug use disorders
studies.key_findings: Supports the use of long-acting stimulants but emphasizes the clinical need for IR 'boosters' in the afternoon for adults to cover late-day impairments, a strategy widely adopted in Canadian clinical practice.

studies.title: ADHD in adults: clinical characteristics and intensity of symptoms in 1,100 Norwegian patients
studies.key_findings: Detailed the clinical treatment of 1,100 Norwegian adults, showing that many required doses and regimens that were off-label relative to pediatric guidelines, including split doses for better symptom control.

studies.title: Trends in ADHD medication use: a 10-year follow-up of Icelandic children
studies.journal_name: Journal of Child and Adolescent Psychopharmacology
studies.dosing_strategy: Preschool off-label use and dosing trends
studies.key_findings: Found a dramatic increase in methylphenidate use in Iceland. It notes that a proportion of prescriptions were for preschool-aged children (off-label) and that multiple daily dosing was common for IR formulations.
